questions.question: Where do personal skills live and how do they differ from project skills?
options: Personal skills live in ~/.claude/skills and follow you across all projects, while project skills live in .claude/skills inside a repository and are shared with anyone who clones it
Personal skills live in .claude/skills inside a repository, while project skills live in ~/.claude/skills and are only available on Windows
Personal skills live in C:/Users/<your-user>/.claude/skills on all operating systems, while project skills live in ~/.claude/skills
Personal skills and project skills both live in the same location but are distinguished by file naming conventions
questions.explanation: Personal skills in ~/.claude/skills follow you across projects, while project skills in .claude/skills are repository-specific and shared with clones.

questions.question: How do skills differ from CLAUDE.md files in terms of when they load into conversations?
options: Skills load into every conversation like CLAUDE.md files do
Skills load on demand when they match your request, while CLAUDE.md files load into every conversation
CLAUDE.md files load on demand, while skills load into every conversation automatically
Both skills and CLAUDE.md files require explicit invocation through slash commands
questions.explanation: Skills load on demand only when Claude detects a matching request, whereas CLAUDE.md files load into every conversation regardless of task.

questions.question: According to the class content, what is the primary indicator that you need to create a skill?
options: When you need to use a slash command more than once
When you find yourself explaining the same thing to Claude repeatedly
When you want Claude to use TypeScript's strict mode
When you need to update your CLAUDE.md file
questions.explanation: The class explicitly states that if you find yourself explaining the same thing to Claude repeatedly, that's a skill waiting to be written.

questions.question: Which two fields are required when configuring skill metadata in the SKILL.md frontmatter?
options: name and description
name and allowed-tools
description and model
allowed-tools and model
questions.explanation: The class content explicitly states that 'name (required)' and 'description (required)' are the two required fields, while allowed-tools and model are optional.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the allowed-tools field in skill configuration?
options: To specify which Claude model version to use for the skill
To restrict which tools Claude can use when the skill is active for security or read-only workflows
To define the maximum context window size for the skill
To list all the external APIs the skill can access
questions.explanation: The class content states that 'allowed-tools restricts which tools Claude can use when the skill is active — useful for read-only or security-sensitive workflows.'

questions.question: What is progressive disclosure and what is the recommended maximum size for SKILL.md?
options: A method to gradually reveal skill features based on user experience level; maximum 1,000 lines
A technique to keep essential instructions in SKILL.md and put detailed reference material in separate files that Claude reads only when needed; maximum 500 lines
A security protocol that limits Claude's access to sensitive files; maximum 2,000 lines
A file organization system that requires all skill content to be in a single document; maximum 64 characters
questions.explanation: The class content defines progressive disclosure as keeping 'SKILL.md under 500 lines and link to supporting files (references, scripts, assets) that Claude reads only when needed.'

questions.question: What are the two main parts of a SKILL.md file and how are they separated?
options: Header and body sections separated by a blank line
Frontmatter containing metadata and instructions below, separated by dashes (---)
Name section and description section separated by a comma
Configuration and content sections separated by a colon
questions.explanation: The SKILL.md file consists of frontmatter dashes containing the name and description, followed by instructions below the second set of dashes.

questions.question: When Claude Code starts up, what does it load from skills?
options: The complete SKILL.md file content for all skills
Only the skill names and descriptions, not the full content
Only the instructions section of each skill
The directory structure but not the metadata
questions.explanation: Claude Code loads only skill names and descriptions at startup for semantic matching, and only reads the full SKILL.md content after the user confirms loading a matched skill.

questions.question: What is the correct priority order when multiple skills have the same name?
options: Personal → Enterprise → Project → Plugins
Project → Personal → Enterprise → Plugins
Enterprise → Personal → Project → Plugins
Plugins → Project → Personal → Enterprise
questions.explanation: The skill priority hierarchy is Enterprise (highest) → Personal → Project → Plugins (lowest), which allows organizations to enforce standards while enabling individual customization.

questions.question: When should you use CLAUDE.md instead of skills?
options: When you have project-wide standards that should always apply to every conversation
When you need to perform a specific task that only applies sometimes
When you want to run automated operations triggered by file saves
When you need to delegate work to a separate execution context
questions.explanation: CLAUDE.md loads into every conversation and is designed for always-on project standards, while skills load on demand for task-specific expertise.

questions.question: What is the key difference between skills and hooks?
options: Skills are event-driven while hooks are request-driven
Skills are request-driven while hooks are event-driven
Skills run in isolated contexts while hooks share the main conversation context
Skills provide external tools while hooks provide internal knowledge
questions.explanation: Skills activate based on what you're asking (request-driven), while hooks fire on events like file saves or tool calls (event-driven).

questions.question: When should you use subagents instead of skills?
options: When you want to enhance Claude's knowledge for the current task
When you want to delegate a task to a separate execution context with isolation from the main conversation
When you need to validate input before specific tool calls
When you need to provide external tools and integrations
questions.explanation: Subagents run in isolated execution contexts and are used when you want to delegate work independently from the main conversation, unlike skills which add knowledge to the current context.

questions.question: Where should you place skills in your repository so that anyone who clones the repo gets them automatically?
options: .claude/skills
.claude/agents
.claude/plugins
.claude/settings
questions.explanation: Project skills in .claude/skills are shared automatically through Git — anyone who clones the repo gets them without extra installation needed.

questions.question: What is a critical difference between built-in agents and custom subagents regarding skill access?
options: Built-in agents can access skills while custom subagents cannot
Built-in agents cannot access skills at all, while custom subagents can use skills when explicitly listed
Both built-in and custom agents can access all skills automatically
Custom subagents can only access plugin skills, not repository skills
questions.explanation: Built-in agents like Explorer, Plan, and Verify can't access skills at all, while custom subagents can use skills when you explicitly list them in their frontmatter skills field.

questions.question: When would enterprise managed settings be the most appropriate method for distributing skills?
options: When skills are needed only by individual developers working on personal projects
When you want to share skills broadly with the open-source community and external partners
When you need mandatory standards, security requirements, and compliance workflows consistent across the organization
When skills are specific to a single project with limited scope and infrequent updates
questions.explanation: Enterprise managed settings take the highest priority and should be used for mandatory standards, security requirements, compliance workflows, and coding practices that must be consistent across the organization.

questions.question: What is the first troubleshooting step you should take when skills don't work as expected?
options: Use the skills validator tool to catch structural problems
Run chmod +x on all script files
Clear the cache and restart Claude Code
Check if your skill description matches your request phrasing
questions.explanation: The class content explicitly states that you should start with the skills validator tool — it catches structural problems before you spend time debugging other things.

questions.question: What are the exact requirements for a skill's file structure to load correctly?
options: The SKILL.md file can be at the skills root with any capitalization
The SKILL.md file must be inside a named directory and the file name must be exactly SKILL.md with all caps on SKILL and lowercase md
The skill file must be named skill.md and placed directly in the skills folder
The file can be named SKILL.md or Skill.md as long as it's in any subdirectory
questions.explanation: The class content specifies that the SKILL.md file must be inside a named directory (not at the skills root) and the file name must be exactly SKILL.md — all caps on 'SKILL', lowercase 'md'.

questions.question: When a skill doesn't trigger, what is the cause almost always?
options: The skill lacks the required execute permissions in the system configuration
The description lacks semantic overlap with your request phrasing and wording
The plugin cache requires clearing to refresh the skill index
A priority conflict exists between the skill and an enterprise-level skill
questions.explanation: The class content states that when a skill doesn't trigger, the cause is almost always the description — Claude uses semantic matching, so your request needs to overlap with the description's meaning.
